title: Labour Code (2019), Article 1: Probation period
text: An employment contract may provide for a probation period of no more than three months. During the probation period either party may terminate the contract by giving three working days' written notice, without stating a reason. A probation period may not be agreed for employees under 18 or for fixed-term contracts shorter than six months.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 2: Working time and overtime
text: Normal working time shall not exceed 40 hours per week and 8 hours per day. Overtime may be ordered only with the employee's written consent, except in emergencies, and may not exceed 8 hours per week or 180 hours per calendar year. Overtime shall be paid at no less than 1.5 times the employee's hourly rate, or 2 times on public holidays.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 3: Breaks and rest periods
text: An employee who works more than five hours in a day is entitled to an unpaid meal break of at least 30 minutes. Every employee is entitled to a daily rest of at least 11 consecutive hours and an uninterrupted weekly rest of at least 35 hours.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 4: Annual leave
text: Every employee is entitled to at least 20 working days of paid annual leave per year. Employees under 18 and employees with a recognised disability are entitled to 25 working days. Unused leave may be carried over to the following year only by written agreement and must be used within that year.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 5: Pay during sickness
text: For the first two days of temporary incapacity for work the employer shall pay sickness benefit of 80 percent of the employee's average pay. From the third day, sickness benefit is paid by the State Social Insurance Fund. The employee must inform the employer of the incapacity on its first day.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 6: Notice of dismissal by the employer
text: An employer terminating an employment contract without fault of the employee must give written notice of one month if the employee has worked for the employer for less than one year, two months for one to ten years, and three months for more than ten years. The notice periods are doubled for employees raising a child under 14 alone.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 7: Severance pay
text: An employee dismissed without fault shall receive severance pay equal to one month's average salary if employed for less than one year, two months' salary for one to five years, and three months' salary for more than five years. Severance pay is not due when the contract ends on expiry of a fixed term.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 8: Resignation by the employee
text: An employee may terminate an employment contract of indefinite duration by giving the employer 20 calendar days' written notice. The notice period is reduced to three working days if the employer has failed to pay wages for more than two months.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 9: Remote work
text: Remote work may be agreed at the request of either party. The employer must grant a request for remote work from a pregnant employee or an employee raising a child under three years of age unless this would cause the employer disproportionate costs. The employer shall reimburse the agreed costs of equipment and communication needed for remote work.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 10: Parental leave
text: A mother is entitled to 126 calendar days of maternity leave. A father is entitled to 30 calendar days of paternity leave, to be taken at any time before the child reaches one year of age. Either parent may take childcare leave until the child reaches three years of age.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 11: Non-competition agreements
text: A non-competition agreement restricting the employee after termination is valid only if made in writing, limited to a maximum of two years, and the employer pays compensation of at least 40 percent of the employee's average salary for the whole restricted period. An agreement without compensation is void.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 12: Payment of wages
text: Wages shall be paid at least twice a month, unless the employee requests payment once a month in writing. When paying wages, the employer shall provide the employee with a statement of the amounts calculated, paid and deducted.

title: Labour Code (2019), Article 13: Equal pay and non-discrimination
text: Employers shall pay equal wages to women and men for the same work or work of equal value. Discrimination on the grounds of sex, age, disability, ethnic origin, religion or sexual orientation in hiring, pay, promotion or dismissal is prohibited. The burden of proof shifts to the employer once facts suggesting discrimination are presented.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 1: Definitions
text: Personal data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. Processing means any operation performed on personal data, including collection, storage, use, disclosure and erasure. The controller is the person who determines the purposes and means of processing.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 2: Lawful grounds for processing
text: Personal data may be processed only if the data subject has given consent, processing is necessary to perform a contract with the data subject, to comply with a legal obligation, to protect vital interests, to perform a task in the public interest, or for the legitimate interests of the controller where these are not overridden by the rights of the data subject.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 3: Conditions for consent
text: Consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous. The data subject may withdraw consent at any time, and withdrawing must be as easy as giving it. For online services offered directly to a child under 14, consent must be given by the child's parent or guardian.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 4: Right of access
text: The data subject has the right to obtain confirmation whether personal data concerning them is processed and a copy of that data. The controller shall respond within one month of receiving the request; this period may be extended by two further months for complex requests. The first copy shall be provided free of charge.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 5: Right to erasure
text: The data subject has the right to have personal data erased without undue delay where the data is no longer necessary for its purpose, consent has been withdrawn, the data subject has objected to processing, or the data was processed unlawfully. The right does not apply where processing is required by law.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 6: Notification of a personal data breach
text: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall notify the Data Protection Inspectorate without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it. Where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to individuals, the controller shall also inform the affected data subjects without undue delay.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 7: Data protection officer
text: The controller and processor shall designate a data protection officer where processing is carried out by a public authority, where core activities consist of large-scale regular and systematic monitoring of individuals, or where they process special categories of data on a large scale.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 8: Video surveillance at the workplace
text: An employer may use video surveillance at the workplace only to ensure the safety of persons or protect property. Employees must be informed in writing before surveillance starts. Cameras may not be installed in toilets, changing rooms or rest areas. Recordings shall be kept for no longer than 30 days unless needed as evidence.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 9: Direct marketing
text: Electronic direct marketing messages may be sent to natural persons only with their prior consent. A customer's email obtained in the course of a sale may be used for marketing similar products if the customer was given a clear opportunity to object. The data subject may object to direct marketing at any time, free of charge.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 10: Transfers to third countries
text: Personal data may be transferred to a country outside the European Economic Area only if that country ensures an adequate level of protection or the controller provides appropriate safeguards such as standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 11: Administrative fines
text: Infringements of this Act may be subject to administrative fines of up to 20 million euros or, for an undertaking, up to 4 percent of its total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher. When deciding on a fine the Inspectorate considers the nature, gravity and duration of the infringement.

title: Personal Data Protection Act (2020), Article 12: Storage limitation
text: Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes of processing. Controllers shall set retention periods for each category of data and review them regularly.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 1: Right of withdrawal from distance contracts
text: A consumer who concludes a contract at a distance, such as online or by telephone, may withdraw from the contract within 14 days without giving any reason. For sales of goods the period begins on the day the consumer receives the goods.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 2: Refund after withdrawal
text: The trader shall reimburse all payments received from the consumer, including standard delivery costs, within 14 days of receiving the notice of withdrawal. The trader may withhold the refund until the goods have been received back or the consumer has supplied proof of having sent them back.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 3: Costs of returning goods
text: The consumer shall bear the direct cost of returning the goods unless the trader has agreed to bear it or failed to inform the consumer that the consumer has to bear it. The consumer is liable for any diminished value of the goods resulting from handling beyond what is necessary to establish their nature and functioning.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 4: Exceptions to the right of withdrawal
text: The right of withdrawal does not apply to goods made to the consumer's specifications or clearly personalised, goods which deteriorate rapidly, sealed goods unsuitable for return for health or hygiene reasons once unsealed, and digital content whose supply has begun with the consumer's express consent.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 5: Legal guarantee of conformity
text: The trader is liable for any lack of conformity of goods which becomes apparent within two years of delivery. Any defect that becomes apparent within one year of delivery is presumed to have existed at the time of delivery, unless the trader proves otherwise.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 6: Remedies for defective goods
text: Where goods are defective, the consumer is first entitled to have them repaired or replaced free of charge. If the trader refuses or does not complete the repair or replacement within 14 days, the consumer may demand a proportionate price reduction or terminate the contract and receive a full refund.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 7: Unfair contract terms
text: A term in a consumer contract which has not been individually negotiated is unfair if it causes a significant imbalance in the parties' rights and obligations to the detriment of the consumer. Unfair terms are not binding on the consumer; the rest of the contract remains in force if it can exist without them.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 8: Price indications and discounts
text: Traders shall display the final price of goods including all taxes. Any announcement of a price reduction shall indicate the prior price, which is the lowest price applied by the trader during the 30 days before the reduction.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 9: Delivery of goods
text: Unless otherwise agreed, the trader shall deliver the goods within 30 days of concluding the contract. If the trader fails to deliver on time, the consumer may set an additional reasonable period, and if the goods are still not delivered, terminate the contract and obtain a refund.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 10: Consumer complaints and dispute resolution
text: A trader shall reply to a consumer's written complaint within 14 days. If the dispute is not resolved, the consumer may apply free of charge to the Consumer Rights Protection Authority for out-of-court dispute resolution within one year of submitting the complaint to the trader.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 11: Automatic renewal of subscriptions
text: Where a subscription contract renews automatically, the trader must remind the consumer at least 30 days before each renewal. After the first year, the consumer may terminate an automatically renewed contract at any time with one month's notice.

title: Consumer Rights Act (2018), Article 12: Gift vouchers
text: Gift vouchers and prepaid cards sold to consumers shall be valid for at least 12 months from the date of purchase. A term providing a shorter validity period is void.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 1: Form of the lease
text: A lease of residential premises for more than one month shall be concluded in writing. The lease shall state the rent, the security deposit, the duration of the lease and the condition of the premises at handover.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 2: Security deposit
text: The security deposit may not exceed two months' rent. The landlord shall return the deposit within 30 days after the end of the lease, deducting only unpaid rent and the documented cost of damage beyond normal wear and tear.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 3: Rent increases
text: The landlord may increase the rent no more than once in 12 months and must give the tenant at least two months' written notice. Rent under a fixed-term lease may be increased only if the lease expressly provides for it.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 4: Landlord's access to the premises
text: The landlord may enter the leased premises only after giving the tenant at least 24 hours' notice and at a reasonable time of day, except in an emergency threatening life or property.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 5: Repairs and maintenance
text: The landlord is responsible for repairs to the structure, heating, plumbing and electrical installations. The tenant is responsible for minor repairs and for damage the tenant caused. If the landlord fails to remedy an urgent defect within 14 days of written notice, the tenant may have it repaired and deduct the reasonable cost from the rent.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 6: Termination by the tenant
text: A tenant may terminate a lease of indefinite duration by giving one month's written notice. A fixed-term lease may be terminated early by the tenant if the landlord materially breaches the lease or, where the lease allows it, with three months' notice.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 7: Termination by the landlord
text: A landlord may terminate a lease of indefinite duration with three months' written notice if the landlord or a close relative needs the premises for their own residence. Where the tenant has failed to pay rent for more than two months, the landlord may terminate the lease with 30 days' written notice.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 8: Eviction
text: A tenant may be evicted only on the basis of a court decision. The landlord may not change the locks, remove the tenant's belongings or disconnect utilities in order to force the tenant to leave.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 9: Subletting
text: The tenant may sublet the premises or part of them only with the landlord's prior written consent. The tenant remains liable to the landlord for the subtenant's obligations.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 10: Utilities and service charges
text: Unless the lease provides otherwise, the tenant pays for metered utilities such as electricity, water and gas. The landlord shall provide the tenant with meter readings and invoices justifying any service charges passed on to the tenant.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 11: Sale of leased premises
text: If leased premises are sold, the lease continues and the new owner assumes the rights and obligations of the landlord. The sale of the premises is not in itself a ground for terminating the lease.

title: Residential Tenancy Act (2017), Article 12: Pets and assistance animals
text: A lease may restrict or prohibit keeping pets. However, a landlord may not refuse to allow a guide dog or other assistance animal needed by a tenant with a disability.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 1: Share capital of a private limited company
text: The minimum share capital of a private limited company is 1,000 euros. The share capital must be fully paid before the company is registered, in money or in kind as valued by an independent expert.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 2: Registration of a company
text: A company is established when it is entered in the Register of Legal Entities. Applications submitted electronically with the required documents shall be processed within five working days.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 3: Duties of directors
text: Directors shall act honestly and in the best interests of the company, with the care of a prudent manager. A director must disclose any conflict of interest and may not vote on transactions in which they have a personal interest. Directors are liable for damage caused to the company by breach of these duties.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 4: Annual financial statements
text: The board shall prepare annual financial statements and submit them to the Register of Legal Entities within five months after the end of the financial year, after approval by the general meeting.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 5: Annual general meeting
text: The annual general meeting of shareholders shall be held within four months after the end of the financial year. Shareholders shall be notified of the meeting at least 14 days in advance, together with the agenda and draft resolutions.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 6: Distribution of dividends
text: Dividends may be paid only from distributable profit shown in approved annual financial statements. No dividend may be paid if, after payment, the company's equity would fall below the sum of its share capital and non-distributable reserves, or if the company is insolvent.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 7: Duty to file for bankruptcy
text: When a company becomes unable to pay its debts as they fall due, its director must file for bankruptcy with the court within 30 days of becoming aware of the insolvency. A director who fails to do so is personally liable to creditors for the resulting damage.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 8: Register of beneficial owners
text: Companies shall identify and register their beneficial owners, meaning natural persons who directly or indirectly own or control more than 25 percent of the shares or voting rights, and keep this information up to date.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 9: Statutory audit
text: A private limited company must have its annual financial statements audited if on the balance sheet date it exceeds two of the following three thresholds: net turnover of 3.5 million euros, total assets of 1.8 million euros, or an average of 50 employees during the financial year.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 10: Voluntary liquidation
text: Shareholders holding at least two thirds of the votes may decide to liquidate the company. The liquidator shall notify all known creditors and publish a notice; assets may be distributed to shareholders only after all creditors have been paid.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 11: Transfer of shares and pre-emption
text: A shareholder wishing to sell shares to a third party must first offer them to the other shareholders, who have a pre-emption right exercisable within 30 days. If the right is not exercised, the shares may be sold to the third party on terms no more favourable than those offered.

title: Companies Act (2016), Article 12: Company records
text: The company shall keep minutes of general meetings and board meetings, the register of shareholders and accounting documents for at least ten years.
